title: Lower the spring roller shade to the tape line
instruction: Lower the shade so its bottom bar stays at the blue tape line.
context: Why: spring roller shades hang in homes, classrooms and offices. The knack: pull it a little past the spot, then let it up slowly until it locks; let go while it moves and it spins to the top. The maker's instructions say so: pull down, hesitate, let it retract very slowly until it locks. It locks only at each half turn and only when turning slowly, so the bar goes below the line by under one catch, against the spring, eases up and is let go once caught. Done by: whoever lives or works with one.
setup: Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table top. Wall section, standing on the table and screwed to it with four steel corner braces (two each side, one in front of the panel and one behind, feet 15 x 2.5 cm, outside the window trim): a 90 x 90 cm panel of 19 mm painted plywood with its room face at x 42, from y -17 to 73. It has a 56 x 64 cm window opening (y 0 to 56, height 8 to 72) with 3 mm white acrylic standing in it as the glass, cased on the room face with 1x4 pine trim (19 x 89 mm). The shade: a Draper Cordless FlexShade spring roller shade, regular roll, outside mount, ordered 61 cm (24 in) wide and 91 cm (36 in) high, with an opaque beige fabric and Draper's small round exposed hem bar (aluminium, plastic end caps, 19 mm across as measured at reset, since Draper lists both 19 and 16 mm; the bar and hanging fabric weigh about 0.3 kg). Its 38 mm aluminium roller tube hangs on Draper's metal brackets, screwed through two 38 mm pine spacer blocks to the head casing, with its axis 76.5 cm up; the hem bar's centre line is at x 34 and the shade spans y -3 to 58. The roller has a spring and a lock that can stop it at each half turn: 6.2 cm of hem-bar travel apart here. The spring's pull at the bar, read on a 10 N spring scale hooked on the bar's middle, is 5.0 N at the start catch and 6.0 N at the line's catch. Start: the shade is caught at the catch whose hem-bar bottom is 31.05 cm above the table (the bar's centre at 32.0 cm), which reads 210.5 mm on both rules. Tape line: 24 mm (0.94 in) blue painter's tape (ScotchBlue 2090) runs level across both side casings, its upper edge 18.65 cm above the table: level with the hem bar's bottom at the second catch below the start (12.4 cm lower; 86.5 mm on the rules). These heights are for a 19 mm bar and 6.2 cm catches: the start reading, tape and rules are set from the catches measured at reset. Two 300 mm steel rules (1 mm graduations) stand upright on the side casings, 7 mm outside each end of the shade, their zero 10 cm above the table. Both arms start in their start pose. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Scored from the trial video (front view, both rules in frame) and the two steel rules. The bar's height is the mean of the two rule readings at the hem bar's bottom. Still means the reading changes less than 2 mm over the last 3 s of the trial; clear means no gripper within 3 cm of the hem bar or the fabric over those 3 s. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full-score state has held for those 3 s. Score 0 if the wall section moves more than 5 mm from its taped marks at any time, or the shade comes out of a bracket, even if put back. Otherwise, at the end: 0 if the bar was never pulled at least 5 cm below its start, or if its bottom is less than 3 cm below its start (back at its start catch, or run up to the top); 0.25 if it was pulled 5 cm down and its bottom is at least 3 cm below its start, but it is not still and clear (still held, touched or moving); 0.5 if it is still and clear and at least 3 cm below its start, but its bottom is more than 3 cm from the tape's upper edge (caught at another catch); 1.0 if it is still and clear with its bottom within 3 cm of the tape's upper edge. Catches are 6.2 cm apart, so a 3 cm band holds only the line's catch. Only the end counts: the shade may run up and be pulled down again within the run limit.
reset_notes: Nothing is used up. Before each trial: raise the shade by hand to its start catch (pull it a little down, let it rise slowly and stop at the catch reading 210.5 mm on both rules, within 2 mm), let go and check it holds; check the wall section, tape and rules are on their marks; put both arms in their start pose. Before the first trial of the day, and with a new shade: read the spring's pull on the 10 N scale at the start catch and at the line's catch (5.0 and 6.0 N, each within 0.5 N; Draper's spring tension is set at the bracket); measure the hem bar's diameter and the catch spacing (the bar's travel between two catches) on the rules, and set the tape and rules from them; and measure the catch speed: raise the bar by hand through a catch at a steady pace, filmed against a rule at 60 fps, and record the fastest rise that still catches and the slowest that runs past. A shade that runs past a catch when let up slowly, or catches when let go fast, is replaced. Run the simulator with -E object_jitter=0 (one fixed layout).
fidelity: Approximate; a real catalogue shade at full size, worked by its hem bar. Fabric: a rigid plate on the bar, which slides straight, 6.2 cm per half turn, a catch each; the roller is a fixed block, not turning. Spring: linear, 5.0 N up at the start, 6.0 N at the line; 0.5 kg moves. Lock: a rule; a bar rising through a catch under 20 mm/s stops (a hidden stop slides in), faster runs on; 5 mm below frees it. Real catch speed: measured at reset. Bar collides as a 19 mm diamond; wall: free 30 kg body.
